target.title: fix(nodes-camera): add timeout to URL media downloads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Node camera URL-backed media downloads used the guarded fetch path but did not provide a request deadline. If the node host accepted the connection and never sent headers or completed the response, `writeUrlToFile` could wait indefinitely while saving camera artifacts.

## Why This Change Was Made
This PR adds a 120s deadline to `writeUrlToFile`'s guarded fetch call, while leaving the existing HTTPS requirement, node-host match, redirect host validation, body cleanup, and max-byte enforcement intact. Tests can pass a smaller timeout override so the regression proof remains fast.

## User Impact
A stalled node-hosted camera URL now fails through the existing error path instead of wedging the CLI media write.

## Evidence
- Focused test: `pnpm vitest run src/cli/nodes-camera.test.ts` -> 29 passed.
- Format/lint: `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/cli/nodes-camera.ts src/cli/nodes-camera.test.ts && pnpm exec oxlint src/cli/nodes-camera.ts src/cli/nodes-camera.test.ts && git diff --check` -> passed.
- Whitespace: `git diff --check` -> clean.
- Collision check before opening: open PR changed-files query for `src/cli/nodes-camera.ts` returned no open PRs.

## Proof
Real behavior proof: the new regression starts a real local `node:http` server that accepts the request and deliberately never sends response headers. The test points the guarded fetch mock at that real hanging server while still calling `writeUrlToFile` with a production-shaped HTTPS node URL, then verifies the call aborts at a 50ms timeout and leaves no partial file behind.

Red/green property: without passing `timeoutMs` from `writeUrlToFile` into `fetchWithSsrFGuard`, the hanging server request would hit the test's 500ms watchdog instead of rejecting with the guarded timeout.

What was not tested: live node hardware. The test covers the actual hanging server behavior locally and keeps the existing host/protocol validation path in place.

target.title: fix(codex): route internal heartbeat sends through provider
target.body:
Closes #102206

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Codex app-server heartbeat/internal turns could be stamped as `webchat`-bound, causing Discord notification sends from those internal turns to be rejected by the default cross-provider outbound policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

Codex message-tool routing should still prefer the explicit message channel for normal deliverable turns, but the internal `webchat` channel is only a non-delivery source marker for heartbeat-style turns. When Codex receives both `messageChannel: "webchat"` and a deliverable `messageProvider`, this change binds message-tool execution to the deliverable provider instead of the internal marker.

## User Impact

Codex-backed heartbeat notifications can send to the intended provider without requiring users to loosen cross-provider messaging settings globally.

## Evidence

- Deterministic source-level reproduction: current main can pass the internal Codex `webchat` marker as the effective `messageProvider` for heartbeat/internal turns, which leaves Discord-targeted sends subject to the webchat provider policy. The added regression test builds a Codex dynamic-tool context with `messageChannel: "webchat"` and `messageProvider: "discord"` and asserts outbound sends are routed through Discord instead of the internal marker.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-build.test.ts`
  - Result: 1 Vitest shard passed; 52 tests passed.
- `corepack pnpm exec oxfmt --check extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-build.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-build.test.ts`
  - Result: all matched files use the correct format.
- `git diff --check HEAD~1..HEAD`
  - Result: no whitespace errors.
- Secret scan over `git diff HEAD~1..HEAD`
  - Result: pass.

Note: I did not run a live Discord/Codex heartbeat because no live Discord bot/webhook credentials are available in this environment; the proof is the narrowed source-level regression for the provider-selection branch.
